html:
In 1981 Mauritania became the last country in the world to abolish slavery by law, after a decree by the military government.

Hereditary slavery, mostly of black Haratin held by Moorish families, came from the old order of the desert set after the Char Bouba war. The 1981 law set no punishment, and only in 2007 was owning slaves made a crime; special courts followed in 2015. Very few owners have been convicted. Campaigners, such as Biram Dah Abeid of the anti-slavery movement IRA, have been jailed and later ran for president. The Haratin, freed or not, are a large share of the population and press for equal rights. See also the slave trades and Saharan trade.
sum: In 1981 Mauritania became the last country in the world to abolish slavery by law, after a decree by the military government.
